issues.description: The problem statement and the template declare the addParent method with parameter order (Person person, Person parent), but the solution's PersonService defines addParent with the parameters named in the reversed order (Person parent, Person person). While Java method signatures are based on types (so this does not cause a compile error), the swapped parameter naming/order in the solution is inconsistent with the specification and template and may confuse students reading the solution or comparing implementation to the instructions and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the parameters in the solution's PersonService.addParent method to match the problem statement and template signature (Person person, Person parent) and update the implementation variable usage accordingly. This keeps the API semantics aligned and avoids confusion when students compare template, spec, and solution.

issues.description: The conceptual contract for addParent(person, parent) is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement and the template declare addParent(Person person, Person parent) (child first, parent second), and PersonResource calls personService.addParent(person, persistedParent). However, the solution implementation declares the method as addParent(Person parent, Person person) (parameters swapped). This causes a semantic mismatch where calls from PersonResource will pass the child as the first argument but the solution treats the first argument as the parent, effectively reversing the relationship and saving the wrong entity. Students mapping the requirement to the implementation will be confused and the application behaviour will be incorrect.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution method signature and parameter names with the problem statement and template: change the solution implementation to public Person addParent(Person person, Person parent) and use those parameter names in the method body (check parent count on 'person', add 'parent' to person.getParents(), and save 'person'). Alternatively, if intentional, update PersonResource calls and documentation everywhere to match the swapped parameter order, but the clear fix is to restore the expected (person, parent) parameter order in the solution.
